questions.q: Identify the three major personal losses फुज्क्यक suffered before age 40, and state the year his first published poem "तवघ्र की दह" appeared.
questions.a: Correct answer: Mother's death (1918), father's death (shortly after), wife's death (year not specified in intro but implied early 1920s); first poem published in 1916. A wrong answer (e.g., "only mother died" or "first poem in 1922") reveals the student has not distinguished between life events and literary milestones, confusing chronological order — a critical error for tracing artistic development in board answers.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the NCERT introduction mentions फुज्क्यक's editorship of "लेउो;" (1922) and "एरोक्यक" (1923–24) alongside his creative writing.
questions.a: Correct answer: These editorial roles placed him at the center of the Hindi literary public sphere, exposing him to contemporary debates (Chhayavad vs. pragativad), expanding his linguistic repertoire, and forcing disciplined engagement with language — all of which refined his poetic craft. A wrong answer ("just jobs he did") misses the causative link between editorial work and poetic innovation, a connection explicitly tested in CBSE "author's contribution to literature" long-answer questions.

questions.q: The introduction states: "फुज्क्यक की काव्य-भाषा के विविध रूप और स्तर हैं।" Give ONE concrete example from the text of this linguistic range, naming the specific work and the register used.
questions.a: Correct answer: "राम की शक्ति पूजा" uses highly Sanskritised, classical register (तत्सम-प्रधान), while "कुकुरमुत्ता" employs colloquial, rustic Avadhi/Bhojpuri-inflected Hindi (देशज-प्रधान). A student who cannot name a specific work and its register has not internalised the evidence-based claim — a gap that leads to vague, unsupported statements in board exams like "he used many styles."

questions.q: Compare फुज्क्यक's thematic preoccupations as listed in the introduction (Indian history, mythology, contemporary life, existential questions) with the typical Chhayavad concerns (nature, love, mysticism, individualism). What does this comparison reveal about his poetic evolution?
questions.a: Correct answer: फुज्क्यक begins within Chhayavad (early poems like "तवघ्र की दह") but expands beyond its self-centred lyricism to engage collective history ("राम की शक्ति पूजा"), social satire ("कुकुरमुत्ता"), and metaphysical inquiry ("सरोज-स्मृति"). This shows a trajectory from subjective romanticism to objective humanism — a paradigm shift examiners expect students to articulate in "development of poet's consciousness" questions.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "फुज्क्यक की कविताओं में भारतीय ग्रामीण जीवन का चित्रण केवल भावुकता के लिए है, यथार्थपरक नहीं।" Use evidence from the introduction to support your judgment.
questions.a: Correct evaluation: The claim is false. The introduction explicitly states: "भारतीय ग्रामीण जीवन से उनका लगाव उनकी अनेक कविताओं में व्यक्त हुआ है" and links it to "आधुनिक जीवन के विभिन्न पहलुओं का चित्रण" — indicating documentary realism alongside emotional resonance. Works like "कुकुरमुत्ता" satirise rural power structures. A student agreeing with the claim confuses Chhayavad's general tendency with फुज्क्यक's specific practice, losing marks for textual evidence.

questions.q: Using only the biographical details in the introduction, draft a 4-line Hindi poem (any metre) that फुज्क्यक *might* have written in 1925, reflecting his then circumstances. Incorporate at least two proper nouns from the text.
questions.a: Expected criteria: Poem must reference (a) Kolkata (बय्गककन) or a magazine (लेउो;/एरोक्यक), (b) personal loss (mother/wife), (c) use first-person voice, (d) show awareness of literary labour. Example: "बय्गककन की धुंध में लेउो; का संपादक / माँ-पत्नी की स्मृति लिए बैठा अकेला / शब्द तराशता हूँ, नहीं कोई सहारा / यही मेरी पूजा, यही मेरा खेला।" A poor answer (generic nature imagery, no biographical anchors) shows the student cannot synthesise life-text connections — the core skill for "creative response" board questions.
